title: Strategy calibration playbook and stakeholder commitments for monthly alignment
creator: Marina Koh
description:
Purpose: Produce a concise, decision-focused packet for the monthly executive alignment that (1) synthesizes initiative health across OKRs, (2) surfaces trade-offs and contingency lanes for resource reallocation, and (3) captures clear stakeholder commitments and escalation triggers. This ticket covers the PM-led synthesis, vetting with Eng and Design, and finalizing a one-page decision slate + 2-slide backup for execs.

Scope:
- One-page executive summary summarizing top 6 initiatives by impact and risk.
- Decision lanes with recommended actions (commit / hold / reallocate) for each initiative.
- Contingency triggers and associated on-call owners.
- Ask ladder (minimal ask, stretch ask) for each initiative where we request additional headcount or budget.
- Appendix: short evidence links (telemetry dashboards, customer tickets, benchmark runs, GitHub PRs, and eval regressions).

Why this is different: Existing readouts are broad; this deliverable is explicitly a calibration playbook that translates signals into actionable commit/halt lanes for the exec committee and engineering leadership. We emphasize clear asks and defined escalation triggers so the exec can sign off during a 20-minute slot.

Audience: CEO, CTO, Head of Product, Eng leads, Design lead, Finance rep.

Deliverables: one-page decision slate (PDF), 2-slide backup, Confluence calibration notes, and a short Loom recording walking through the recommended lanes.
acceptance_criteria: One-page decision slate uploaded to Confluence under /playbooks/q2-calibration and shared with execs
Two-slide backup that includes 1) initiative health + metrics and 2) recommended action lanes for each initiative
All recommendations have a named owner, escalation trigger, and minimal/stretch ask with estimated cost/effort
Feedback from Eng and Design incorporated in an comments section and signed off by leads (comments documented)
Loom recording (5–7 min) posted and linked in the Confluence page
